irregular_checks.question_plain: Do the boundaries enclose four complete bars rather than stems or split bars?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. Internal strokes at crop x 481, 794 and 1071 traverse both staves and the gap; chord stems remain attached to their noteheads and beams within the bars. P067 and P068 each contain six successive upper-staff eighth-note attacks. P069 and P070 each have three eighth notes followed by a dotted quarter note in the main voice; their secondary rests and eighth notes fill the same six eighth-note units. Both outer barlines are complete.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does the crop contain the system’s essential musical ink?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The rectangle at page [102,462,1489,794] encloses the clefs, articulations, diminuendo, piano mark, accents and slurs. A small fingering fragment at the bottom belongs to the following system; no essential ink of system 14 is clipped.

irregular_checks.where: P005/P006 and P030/P031 across system and page boundaries
irregular_checks.question_plain: Are the short regions and repeat boundaries coherent?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. P005 and P006 each contain three eighth-note units, as do P030 and P031. Each neighboring pair totals six eighth-note units. P005 closes with a double barline; P006 starts the repeat, and P030 closes it. These are separately bounded partial regions, not unclosed bars split across systems. The piece begins with a full bar and ends with a full bar.

irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. All sixteen changes are individually addressed in the inventory, including the end-of-region cautionary glyphs in P005, P018, P068, P100 and P101. Repeated opening clefs agree with the preceding effective changes. No frozen-summary contradiction is visible.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Is the terminal region complete and closed?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The opening eighth note, two eighth rests, quarter rest and final eighth rest fill six eighth-note units, and the final heavy barline closes both staves.
